title: One Open Builder Extended Rate Lock per Purchase Agreement
content:
**Condition.** A buyer may hold up to 2 Builder Extended Rate Locks at once in status requested, locked or expired, and at most one of them for any one purchase agreement. A lock is requested only for a purchase agreement with no other lock in status requested, locked or expired.

## What is counted

- The locks counted are the buyer's Builder Extended Rate Locks on the **same purchase agreement** as the lock being requested, in status requested, locked or expired, at the moment of the request; the lock being handled is not counted against itself.
- The authority is the system record of the locks — their purchase agreement and their status — not the buyer's account of them. The record checked is the one tied to the purchase agreement named on the request.

## Condition, judgement, result

| Other lock on the same purchase agreement | Its status | A lock may be requested for that agreement under this condition |
|---|---|---|
| None | — | Yes |
| One or more | requested, locked or expired | No |
| One or more, none of them requested, locked or expired | funded, cancelled or withdrawn | Yes |

The table restates the condition only; the request must still meet every other rule of the Builder Extended Rate Lock.

## Points of judgement

**A buyer holds a locked lock on one agreement and asks for a lock on a second agreement.** The one-per-agreement condition looks only at the second agreement; the buyer's total of open locks across agreements stays within 2.

**An agreement's earlier lock expired and was not relocked.** An expired lock is still in status expired and counts; while it stands in that status no other lock is requested for the same agreement.
